packets.responsibility: Eleven inline-SVG string constants plus two id-suffixed SVG-string factory functions, replacing an earlier Material Symbols icon-font codepoint scheme across every layer-row/Elements-panel icon in the app — chosen specifically because the embedded font is a subsetted build containing only already-referenced codepoints, so an unreferenced glyph renders silently blank.
behavior: 3-line lead-in comment (5710-5712): real icon-handoff SVGs (v5) replace Material Symbols codepoints — no risk of a codepoint missing from the subsetted embedded font; cross-references 'the lock-icon comment below' (timeline.js:6454-6457, out of scope, the actual bug narrative: Material Symbols' `lock_open` codepoint wasn't in the subset and rendered totally blank).
`ICO_EYE` (5713): open-eye outline + solid pupil circle, `stroke-width=1.8`.

8-line comment (5714-5721): v11 added a distinct closed-eye icon for the hidden state instead of dimming the same open-eye glyph via `.off`, so 'hidden' reads at a glance; v14 added an explicit `fill="currentColor"` because SVG's own spec default fill (black) was silently overriding the CSS `color` this icon is meant to follow (`.lico.off{color:var(--text-dark)}`), which is exactly why the closed-eye icon had rendered solid black instead of the dim gray every other 'off' icon uses.
`ICO_EYE_CLOSED` (5722): a single multi-segment `fill="currentColor"` path (crossed-out-eye glyph).
`ICO_LOCK` (5723): filled rounded body rect + open-shackle stroke path.
`ICO_UNLOCK` (5724): identical body, shackle path rotated open (`M8 11V8a4 4 0 017.6-1.8`).

4-line comment (5725-5728): 3D layer toggle (2026-07-28, After-Effects-style) — isometric cube wireframe, plain inline SVG like every other row icon, not an icon-font glyph, per this project's own subsetted-font constraint (CLAUDE.md).
`ICO_3D` (5729): isometric cube outline (hexagon perimeter path + three internal edges).
3-line comment (5730-5732): Mograph duplicator toggle (2026-07-29) — 2×2 grid of squares, one filled (the seed) and three outlined (the copies), same inline-SVG convention as `ICO_3D`.
`ICO_DUP` (5733): four `<rect>` elements, one `fill=currentColor` (seed) and three `fill=none stroke=currentColor` (copies).

4-line comment (5734-5737): Elements panel (2026-08, shapes-panel.js) group/raster-entry icons, same inline-SVG convention, replacing text/emoji glyphs (▤/🖼) that were font/emoji-rendering-dependent — quotes Cyril: "les icônes aussi sont flat design ?".
2-line comment (5738-5739): frame-corner brackets for 'group' — the same shorthand Figma's own layers panel uses for a group row.
`ICO_GROUP` (5740): four corner-bracket path segments, `stroke-linecap/linejoin=round`.
`ICO_IMAGE` (5741): rounded-rect frame + small filled circle (sun) + a mountain-silhouette path.

8-line comment (5742-5751): Combined Shape mode icons (2026-08, Elements panel group row) — EXACT SAME markup as the toolbar's own `#btn-combine-*` buttons (index.html), copied verbatim (not read from the DOM) so the panel's indicator always matches the toolbar even though they are two separate elements; `ICO_COMBINE_NONE` is new (the toolbar itself has no 'no combine' button) — two plain outlined circles, no fill relationship, for `combineMode==='none'`.
`ICO_COMBINE_UNITE` (5752): two overlapping filled circles via a single compound `<path>` (non-zero fill-rule, both circle interiors solid).
`ICO_COMBINE_EXCLUDE` (5753): the identical two-circle compound path with `fill-rule="evenodd"` — the overlap punches out instead of merging.
`ICO_COMBINE_NONE` (5754): two separate outlined circles, `opacity=0.55`, no shared path/mask/clip.

5-line comment (5755-5759): Subtract/Intersect reference an SVG `<mask>`/`<clipPath>` by id — a plain constant string would collide the instant two-or-more groups show this icon at once (duplicate DOM ids resolve to whichever element the browser finds first, silently rendering the WRONG icon on every group after the first); solved by functions taking a caller-supplied unique suffix.
2-line comment continuation (5760-5761): group-bridge.js/shapes-panel.js pass the group's own `gid`, already unique per document by construction.

`icoCombineSubtract(uid)` (5762): builds `m='ic-csub-'+uid`, returns an SVG with a `<mask id=m>` (white filled circle minus black filled circle) applied to a `currentColor` circle, plus an outlined second circle at `opacity=0.45`.

`icoCombineIntersect(uid)` (5763): builds `c='ic-cint-'+uid`, returns an SVG with a `<clipPath id=c>` (second circle) applied to a `currentColor` first circle, plus two outlined circles at `opacity=0.4`.

packets.responsibility: Opens a small predefined-swatch popover ('nuancier') anchored under a layer's colour dot, so a colour change is one click against `LAYER_COLOR_PALETTE` (app.js:375) instead of the full SV/hue/hex `ColorPicker`; a trailing '+' cell falls through to that full picker for an arbitrary custom colour.
behavior: 6-line lead-in comment (5764-5769 minus the declaration line): v5 predefined-swatch picker instead of jumping straight to the full picker; reuses `LAYER_COLOR_PALETTE` (app.js) so the choices match the colours new layers already auto-get (`nextLayerColor`, app.js:376); a '+' cell falls through to the full picker.
Function declaration (5769): `function openLayerColorSwatches(anchorEl,currentHex,onPick){`.
Stale-popover removal (5770): `var old=document.getElementById('layer-color-swatches');if(old)old.remove();` — at most one instance of this popover exists at a time.
Popover shell (5771): creates a `div#layer-color-swatches.lcs-pop`.

Swatch loop (5772-5777): `LAYER_COLOR_PALETTE.forEach(...)` builds one `button.lcs-swatch` per palette colour, marking the currently-selected one with a `.sel` class via a case-insensitive hex compare (5773), sets `style.background`/`title` to the hex, and wires `click` (5775) to `e.stopPropagation();onPick(hex);pop.remove();` — dismissing the popover on pick.

Custom '+' cell (5778-5780): a `button.lcs-swatch.lcs-custom` with text `'+'`, whose click (5779) removes this popover and calls `window.ColorPicker.open(anchorEl,currentHex,onPick)` (color-picker.js:276, out of scope) — the SAME `onPick` callback the caller supplied, so both paths converge on one write site in the caller.

Insertion and positioning (5781-5784): appends `pop` to `document.body`, then clamps its left position to stay on-screen (`Math.min(r.left,window.innerWidth-pop.offsetWidth-8)`) and places it just below the anchor (`r.bottom+4`).

Outside-click dismissal (5785-5789): deferred via `setTimeout(...,0)` (so the triggering click itself doesn't immediately close the popover it just opened) — registers a one-shot `mousedown` listener on `document` that removes `pop` and itself when the click lands outside it.

packets.responsibility: Two behaviours hung off the one colour dot every layer row already has (2026-09, feedback #776, quoted in-source): assign a picked colour to the whole current multi-selection when the clicked row is part of it, and Shift+click a dot to select every layer sharing that same colour — mirroring After Effects' own label-colour column, shared verbatim by Animation 2D's rows (`renderLayerList`) and Motion's (`motion.js`).
behavior: 9-line lead-in comment (5791-5799, split across two comment blocks): introduces both behaviours as a pair hung off the same dot, both already present in AE's own label column; shared by Animation 2D and Motion 'because it is the same control on the same layers seen from two views.'

3-line comment (5799-5802) directly preceding `layerColorTargets`: a colour picked while several layers are selected AND the clicked row is one of them paints the WHOLE selection; a dot clicked outside the selection still means just that one layer — otherwise recolouring one row's dot would silently repaint layers the user forgot were selected.

`layerColorTargets(li)` (5803-5805): `return (_layerSel.length>1&&_layerSel.indexOf(li)>=0)?_layerSel.slice():[li];` — the ENTIRE targeting rule is membership in the current explicit multi-selection (`_layerSel`, declared in C19q's scope, timeline.js:5423, out of scope): there is no automatic cascade to a folder's members or a component's instances beyond whatever the user has already selected via `_layerSel` — a folder row or a component instance is targeted only if it is itself one of the selected indices, identically to any other layer.

`applyLayerColor(li,hex)` (5806-5813): resolves `targets=layerColorTargets(li)` (5807); `pushUndoLayers()` (5808, BEFORE any mutation); `targets.forEach(function(i){if(state.layers[i])state.layers[i].color=hex;})` (5809) — the sole document write, one `.color` field per targeted layer index, guarded by an existence check; `renderLayerList();renderTimeline();` (5810); a toast (5811) `SM.t('toastLayerColorApplied').replace('{n}',targets.length)` only `if(targets.length>1)` — a single-layer recolour is silent; returns `targets.length` (5812).

2-line comment (5814-5815) directly preceding `selectLayersByColor`: Shift+click on a dot selects every layer wearing that same colour, so a label doubles as a saved selection (quotes the feedback: "les personnages en rouge").
